senses.gloss: To declare; to assert, affirm.
The name of the Latin script letter A/a.
A period into which a year is divided, historically based on the phases of the moon.
An exclamation to get attention.
Any natural satellite of a planet.
Used to acknowledge a small mistake or accident.
An expression in sympathy at another's pain.
(Greek god) The goddess of the Moon.
To sell at an auction.
rule made by a local authority
The aggregate of past events, both unrecorded and recorded.
The addition to a writing, inscription, coin, etc., which specifies the time (especially the day, month, and year) when the writing or inscription was given, executed, or made.
The previous experiences and life of a person, specifically (narratology, especially in, _, film, television) a character in a dramatic work.
A device measuring the time of day by the position of a shadow cast by a pole or plate (gnomon) upon an engraved series of marks.
To move the foot in walking; to advance or recede by raising and moving one of the feet to another resting place, or by moving both feet in succession.
(intransitive) To step or walk (on or across something); to trample.
(transitive, of a male) To father; to beget.
To mate; used of a ram mating with a ewe.
A poisonous North American plant, Phytolacca americana, with reddish stems, broad leaves, clusters of white flowers, and dark purple berries.
A building used for something other than a residence (typically with qualifying word).
committee that leads or governs

In many countries, the legislative branch of government, a deliberative assembly or set of assemblies whose elected or appointed members meet to debate the major political issues of the day, make, amend, and repeal laws, authorize the executive branch of government to collect and spend money, and in some cases exercise judicial powers; a legislature.
A legislative body.
A council, assembly, or public meeting, in some Muslim countries or territories.
To deceive using a disguise; to bewile, dupe, mislead.
nautical: book in which details from journey are recorded
One side of a paper leaf in a bound document.

A piece of paper, usually rectangular, that has been prepared for writing, artwork, drafting, wrapping, manufacture of packaging (boxes, envelopes, etc.), and for other uses. The word does not include scraps and irregular small pieces destined to be recycled, used for stuffing or cushioning or paper mache, etc. In modern books, each sheet of paper is typically folded in half, to produce two leaves and four pages. In the absence of folding, "leaf" and "sheet" are equivalent.
Permission or license to pass, or to go and come.
A distinguishable part of a sequence or cycle occurring over time.
Enclosed path of an electric current, usually designed for a certain function.
A kind of hanging bandage put around the neck, in which a wounded arm or hand is supported.
An event for the purpose of tasting and evaluating wine.
(transitive) To treat someone, or something roughly or badly.
To describe or depict with words or gestures.
(mostly, science fiction) A levitating board that can be ridden in the manner of a surfboard or skateboard.
Any substance that has a distinctive smell, especially one added to something (such as household gas) for safety purposes
Not new; previously owned and used by another.
Intent, determined (to do something).
Firm, unyielding, determined.
The act of surveying; a general view.
(in extended senses of the above) A mass of people, a mob or muster, considered as a head count.
The action of asking questions; a survey; an inquiry.

The chemical element (symbol C) with an atomic number of 6. It can be found in pure form for example as graphite, a black, shiny and very soft material, or diamond, a colourless, transparent, crystalline solid and the hardest known material.
A charred substance.
A short break in the action of a sport, for substitution, consultation, etc.
An action of stopping; interruption of travel.
Any relief from exertion; a state of quiet and relaxation.
A temporary stop or rest; an intermission of action; interruption; suspension; cessation.
temporary stoppage of an activity — see also break, pause
An interval of time required by the Roman Catholic Church between the attainment of different degrees of an order.
A mythological creature (usually humanoid and undead) said to feed on the blood or life energy of the living.
Lacking in force (usually strength) or ability.
Rendered less effective.
Deficient in physical strength.
The bottom of a face, (specifically) the typically jutting jawline below the mouth.
One of the bones, usually bearing teeth, which form the framework of the mouth.
(archaic, often, in the plural) The jaw.
The lower edge of the side of the face (below the cheek), defined by the jawbone.
The jaw, jawbone; especially one of the lateral parts of the mandible.
treatment of disease
someone or something that translates meaning from one language to another
A person or thing that interprets the meaning of something for another

A geographic region in Southeast Europe in the Balkans which includes the Republic of North Macedonia, the region of Macedonia in Greece, the Pirin region of Bulgaria, and small parts of Albania and Serbia.
Permeable to some things and not to others, as a cell membrane which allows some molecules through but blocks other substances.
A device intended to explode when stepped upon or touched, or when approached by a ship, vehicle, or person.
The action or progress of wasting; extravagant consumption or ineffectual use.
Seemingly; in appearance.
A foul ball, a ball which has been hit outside of the base lines.
Unsolicited bulk electronic messages.
Learned in the ways of civilized society; civilized; refined.
(UK, Ireland, Australia, mildly, _, vulgar, colloquial) Drunk.
Part of a body.
A violent wind in the form of a mobile, rapidly rotating, funnel cloud that has contacted the ground.
A flexible tube conveying water or other fluid.
(anatomy) An elongated tube from the head or connected to the mouth, of an animal.
A colloquial word or phrase; a common spoken expression.
A whirlwind that forms over water, not associated with a mesocyclone of a thunderstorm (contrary to a true tornado).
(architecture) A structure constructed between two adjacent walls to aid in the transition from a polygonal to a circular structure, as when a dome is constructed on top of a square room.
Having an acrid taste (usually from a basic substance).
One side of a paper leaf in a bound document.
Having, or pertaining to, a tendency to fidget; restless.
The state of being, existing, or occurring; beinghood.
A solid upright structure designed usually to support a larger structure above it, such as a roof or horizontal beam, but sometimes for decoration.

Part of the large intestine; the final segment of the digestive system, after (distal to) the ileum and before (proximal to) the rectum. (Because the colon is the largest part of the large intestine (constituting most of it), it is often treated as synonymous therewith in broad or casual usage.)
A mechanical device with evenly-shaped blades that turn on a shaft to push against air or water, especially one used to propel an aircraft or boat.

(video games) A sandbox video game, released in 2011, in which players explore a three-dimensional world made of blocks and can craft items, build structures, fight mobs to get experience points, enchant items and defeat bosses to earn rewards.
(nautical) A timber or steel bar extending from the keel to the main deck at the stern of a vessel.
An archangel associated in Judaism, Christianity and Islam, with carrying messages from God.
Complete, absolute, full.
To the furthest or most extreme extent; absolute, complete, total, unconditional. [from 15th c.]
(Northumbria) Very, considerably; quite, rather.
The penis.
Any of the genus Naja of venomous snakes that can spread their neck ribs into a broad hood when threatened; a true cobra.
Relating to the Basque people or their language.
Expected or scheduled to take place in the future.
A similar brown liquid obtained from coal tar used as a wood preservative.
Of or pertaining to Heaven, the eternal celestial abode of God or the gods.
Of, relating to, or located in the sky or outer space, where the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars are visible.
(anthropology) The branch of anthropology that scientifically describes specific human cultures and societies.
Of, related to, or suffering from psychosis.
Material, made from the polished skin of a calf, sheep, goat or other animal, used like paper for writing.
A writing paper of very high quality.
A country in Central Africa. Official name: Republic of Cameroon. Capital: Yaoundé. It also claims Ambazonia.
Not experiencing sexual attraction; lacking interest in or desire for sex.
(constellation) A winter constellation of the northern sky, said to resemble a charioteer. It includes the star Capella.
A dining area in an institution where meals may be purchased (as above), provided, or brought in from elsewhere.
small cafeteria or snack bar
A city in Cyprus, known in antiquity as the birthplace of Aphrodite.
A plucked stringed instrument with a triangular body, short neck and three strings, of Russian origin.
A woman who serves in a bar.
The capital city of Serbia; the former capital of Yugoslavia; the former capital of Serbia and Montenegro.
of or relating to the encephalon
A device used to prevent an animal from biting or eating, which is worn on its snout.
The doctrine that all actions are determined by the current state and immutable laws of the universe, with no possibility of choice.
To cut finely, for example slices of meat.
A person skilled at carpentry, the trade of cutting and joining timber in order to construct buildings or other structures.
Of a doctrine, information, etc.: suitable to be imparted to the public without secrecy or other reservations.
A unified fundamental force that combines the aspects of electricity and magnetism and is one of the four fundamental forces.
Applied to a case expressing means or agency, generally corresponding to the English use of prepositions such as by, with, through, or by means of with the objective case.

(constellation) A spring constellation of the northern sky (and autumn of the southern sky) with the outline of a centaur. It includes the stars Alpha Centauri (Rigil Kentaurus and Toliman), Proxima Centauri, and Hadar.
A method of human thought that involves thinking in a linear, step-by-step manner about how a problem can be solved. Logic is the basis of many principles including the scientific method.
A person who basks in the sun to get a tan.
idol
A small carved or molded figure; a statuette.
Administration; the use of limited resources combined with forecasting, planning, leadership and execution skills to achieve predetermined specific goals.
The act of administering; government of public affairs; the service rendered, or duties assumed, in conducting affairs; the conducting of any office or employment; direction.
A city in central Greece, the capital city of Boeotia and an important political centre in antiquity.
To call upon divine or supernatural power to send injury upon; to imprecate evil upon; to execrate.
mythical beast
A halogenated hydrocarbon, trichloromethane, CHCl₃; it is a volatile, sweet-smelling liquid, used extensively as a solvent and formerly as an anesthetic.
To write or say the letters that form a word or part of a word.

A mythological bird, said to be the only one of its kind, which lives for 500 years and then dies by burning to ashes on a pyre of its own making, ignited by the sun. It then arises anew from the ashes.

A statistical measure defined as scriptstyle operatorname Cov(X,Y)= operatorname E((X-μ)(Y-ν)) given two real-valued random variables X and Y, with expected values scriptstyle E(X),=,μ and scriptstyle E(Y),=,ν.
(Christianity) Of or pertaining to the theology of Martin Luther (1483–1546) or his followers, or the Lutheran church.
Specifically, giving indication of a coming ill; being an evil omen
An implement for washing floors or similar, made of a piece of cloth, or a collection of thrums, or coarse yarn, fastened to a handle.
Ground ploughed and harrowed but left unseeded for one year.
A professional who counsels people, especially on personal problems.
To make more moist.
Either of two very large amounts:
Any substance that produces fever, or a rise in body temperature
(chemistry, physics) The separation of positive and negative charges in a nucleus, atom, molecule or system.
An anticonvulsant drug used for neuropathic pain and as an adjunct therapy for seizures.
A small device, especially an electrode, used to explore, investigate or measure something by penetrating or being placed in it.
(sometimes, humorous) Expressing contempt, disgust, or bad temper.
(euphemistic) An expression of disbelief or exasperation.
(slang) An imitation of the sound of gagging, used to express disgust or disdain.
Indicating disapproval, scoffery, irritation, impatience or disbelief. [from 17th c.]
device that controls the flow of a gas or fluid
Causing irritation or annoyance; troublesome; vexatious.
(nautical) Water which collects in the bilges of a ship.
Any of various small to medium-sized breeds of gun dog having a broad muzzle, long, wavy fur and long ears that hang at the side of the head, bred for flushing and retrieving game.
Not circumcised, intact.

A white-bodied, wood-consuming insect of the infraorder Isoptera, in the order Blattodea.
(chemistry) A mixture of a metal and a metal oxide capable of producing a thermite reaction, such as aluminium metal and ferric oxide; used in incendiary devices.
Something that has been transcribed, including:
An athletics event in which contestants compete in swimming, cycling and running in turn.
The way in which something is positioned vis-à-vis its surroundings.
A chronological mistake; the erroneous dating of an event, circumstance, or object.
An ancient Eastern Old Iranian language that was used to compose the sacred hymns and canon of the Zoroastrian Avesta.

Any of a number of flowering plants in the family Zygophyllaceae, including several members of the genus Kallstroemia and the species Tribulus terrestris, native to warm temperate and tropical regions.
aquatic mammal
